drivingQuestion: Why may a widow not be betroth during her mourning if betrothal is permitted in a stricter mourning period?
outcomeNote: the challenge is taken up in the following unit

segments.he: חוּץ מִן הָאַלְמָנָה וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאָסוּר לְכַבֵּס, מוּתָּר לֵיאָרֵס. מְקוֹם שֶׁמּוּתָּר לְכַבֵּס — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁמּוּתָּר לֵיאָרֵס?!
segments.en: § The mishna states that Rabbi Yosei says: All women may be betrothed within three months «except for a widow,» due to the mourning period she must observe for her deceased husband. «Rav Ḥisda» questioned the mishna’s ruling and «said:» Based on an «a fortiori» inference, it should be permitted for a woman to be betrothed during the thirty-day mourning period for her husband: If during another period of mourning, which the Gemara will specify, «when it is prohibited to launder» clothes, «it is permitted to be betrothed,» then during the thirty-day mourning period for a husband, «when it is permitted to launder» clothes, «isn’t it logical that it» should also be «permitted to be betrothed?»

moves.summary: a fortiori, a widow should be permitted to betroth
moves.about: by a fortiori a widow should be permitted to betroth during her thirty days

edges.about: by a fortiori a widow should be permitted to betroth during her thirty days

positions.claim: all women may be betrothed except a widow, due to mourning
a widow should be permitted by a fortiori
positions.basis: betrothal is permitted when laundering is forbidden
